title: Machine learning powered financial credit scoring: a systematic literature review
authors: Ayari, H.; Guetari, R.; Kraiem, N.
tldr: A systematic review of 63 studies shows ensemble and hybrid ML models consistently outperform traditional methods for credit scoring, while deep learning faces interpretability and data availability constraints.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit scoring models based on logistic regression and scorecards are limited by their assumption of linear relationships and narrow feature sets, failing to capture complex borrower behavioral patterns. The rapid growth of ML techniques for credit scoring has produced a fragmented literature with inconsistent datasets, preprocessing methods, and evaluation metrics.
approach: Conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic literature review with five research questions targeting ML models, strengths, limitations, metrics, trends, and adoption challenges.
Searched four databases (SpringerLink, ACM, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar) for publications from 2018 to 2024, extracting 330 papers and selecting 63 primary studies after quality assessment.
Categorized reviewed studies into traditional ML, deep learning, and ensemble learning groups.
Evaluated model performance using accuracy and AUC across four benchmark datasets: German, Australian, Japanese, and Lending Club.
Applied VOSviewer for bibliometric analysis including bibliographic coupling and keyword co-occurrence.
Examined emerging trends including alternative data sources and explainability methods such as SHAP and LIME.
findings: Ensemble and hybrid ML models consistently outperform traditional single classifiers across all benchmark datasets in credit scoring tasks.
num: 93.16% accuracy achieved by multi-stage ensemble on the Japanese dataset, the highest reported across all benchmark datasets.
num: 92.60% AUC achieved by GA+NN model on the German dataset.
num: 91.70% accuracy and 93.78% AUC achieved by GSCI ensemble model on the Lending Club dataset.
Accuracy and AUC are the most frequently reported metrics (49 and 31 studies respectively) but accuracy alone is misleading for imbalanced credit scoring datasets.
Hybrid and ensemble approaches integrating neural networks, optimization algorithms, or boosting demonstrate consistently superior performance and lower variability.
Traditional models like logistic regression remain competitive when interpretability and transparency are prioritized over raw predictive performance.
Model interpretability through LIME and SHAP has shifted from a technical option to a regulatory and operational requirement in credit scoring.
num: 63 primary studies were selected from 330 extracted papers across four databases for the final systematic review.

definitions.definition: Machine learning, a subfield of AI focused on designing algorithms that enable systems to learn from data.
Deep learning, a subset of ML based on artificial neural networks with multiple layers.
Ensemble learning, a technique integrating multiple learning algorithms to enhance predictive performance.
Logistic regression, a probabilistic classification model estimating binary outcome probability.
Decision tree, a supervised model for regression and classification using tree-like decision rules.
Random forest, an ensemble method aggregating multiple decision trees via bootstrap aggregation.
Support vector machine, a supervised model that separates data using an optimal hyperplane.
K-nearest neighbors, a non-parametric classifier based on distance to nearby data points.
Convolutional neural network, a deep feedforward network for feature extraction and classification.
Long short-term memory, a recurrent neural network architecture for sequential data processing.
Extreme gradient boosting, an ensemble model combining tree models with gradient boosting.
Gradient boosting decision trees, an ensemble method combining weak learners through error minimization.
Artificial neural network, computational models inspired by biological neural structures.
Area under the ROC curve, measuring a model's ability to distinguish between classes.
Synthetic minority oversampling technique, addressing class imbalance in datasets.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, a method quantifying each feature's contribution to predictions.
Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations, providing locally accurate explanations for individual predictions.
International Financial Reporting Standard 9, mandating Expected Credit Loss estimation.
Probability of Default, the likelihood a borrower will fail to meet repayment obligations.
Exposure at Default, the loan amount exposed to credit risk at the time of default.
Loss Given Default, the proportion of unrecovered assets calculated as one minus recovery rate.
Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, measuring a model's discriminatory power in credit scoring.
Geometric mean, a metric balancing sensitivity and specificity for imbalanced datasets.
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, guidelines for conducting systematic reviews.
Systematic literature review, a structured methodology for synthesizing research findings.
Penalised logistic tree regression, combining decision tree rules with logistic regression.
Deep Genetic Hierarchical Network of Learners, combining evolutionary computation, EL, and DL.
Multi-grained cascade forest, a deep forest model processing high-dimensional feature information.
Peer-to-peer lending, a lending model connecting borrowers directly with individual lenders.
Fair Isaac Corporation score, a standardized credit scoring model used by major credit bureaus.

citations.author: Dastile

citations.author: Kumar
citations.claim: Focused on credit scoring in rural finance emphasizing the role of fintech and ML/AI in improving access to underserved populations.

citations.author: Hayashi
citations.claim: Conducted a systematic review on DL in credit scoring highlighting superior performance of Deep Belief Networks over traditional models.

citations.author: Lenka
citations.claim: Analyzed ensemble learning for imbalanced credit scoring datasets exploring SMOTE and feature selection methods including GA-based selection with CatBoost achieving 86.70% accuracy.

citations.author: Markov
citations.claim: Reviewed credit scoring methodologies from 2016 to 2021 highlighting the growing prominence of ensemble models.

citations.author: Kamimura
citations.claim: Conducted a review of 46 studies on optimization methods for credit scoring models identifying logistic regression (13%) and growing trend toward hybrid models (72%).

citations.author: Dumitrescu
citations.claim: Introduced Penalized Logistic Tree Regression achieving best AUC with 92.99% on Australian dataset.

citations.author: Kazemi
citations.claim: Proposed GA and neural networks method achieving highest accuracy 91.91% and AUC 92.60% on Australian dataset.

citations.author: Zhang

citations.author: He

citations.author: Chen
citations.claim: Proposed ensemble model using generalized Shapley value and Choquet integral achieving 94.53% recall and 91.43% AUC on Australian dataset.

citations.author: Bussmann

citations.author: Buchner

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic literature review provides a comprehensive synthesis of 63 studies on ML applications in financial credit scoring from 2018 to 2024.
directly_justifies: Ensemble and hybrid ML models consistently outperform traditional single classifiers across all benchmark datasets.
Hybrid approaches integrating optimization algorithms with neural networks achieve the highest accuracy and AUC scores.
Explainability methods such as SHAP and LIME have shifted from optional technical tools to regulatory requirements.
Alternative data sources including social media and mobile phone usage enhance credit scoring for borrowers without formal credit histories.
Traditional models like logistic regression remain competitive when interpretability and regulatory compliance are prioritized.
limits: The review was confined to four databases potentially missing relevant studies from other sources.
The lack of standardized evaluation metrics across reviewed studies makes direct performance comparisons potentially subjective.
The fast-evolving nature of ML techniques means the review may not capture the most recent advances.
The review does not include a reproducible empirical benchmark experiment to independently validate reported performance figures.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 4 was flagged as highly relevant because the paper comprehensively surveys ML methods for credit scoring. Domain 6 was flagged as highly relevant because the paper reviews multiple predictive modeling approaches. Domain 12 was flagged as highly relevant because the paper provides ranked comparative evaluations. Domain 5 was flagged as contextual because borrower behavioral variables are discussed. Domain 6.B was flagged as contextual because LSTM and sequential models are reviewed though the paper focuses on classification.

limitations: The review was limited to four digital libraries potentially missing relevant studies from other sources.
Lack of standardized evaluation metrics across reviewed studies complicates direct performance comparisons.
The search period (2018-2024) may not capture the most recent advances given the fast-evolving nature of ML.
The review does not independently validate reported performance through reproducible empirical benchmarking.
